key_insight: Choose retrieval-pipeline settings per query (given an accuracy or budget target) to significantly reduce serving cost or meet accuracy goals, instead of using a single hand-tuned pipeline for all queries.
problem_solved: Hand-tuned retrieval agent pipelines waste cost or accuracy because they are static per workload; this work enables per-query configuration selection that unlocks untapped cost–quality tradeoffs.
method: Define a catalog of pipeline configurations (LLM, retriever, #documents, #hops, synthesis strategy) and a constrained objective: minimize cost subject to accuracy target or maximize accuracy under a budget.
Map a natural-language query and a target (accuracy or budget) to the best configuration via a query-conditioned selection mechanism (learned predictor or policy over the catalog).
Evaluate and select configurations using predicted cost/accuracy tradeoffs to choose the cheapest configuration that meets accuracy (or the most accurate within budget).
impact: Enables retrieval-agent deployments to automatically adapt per request, lowering inference cost and/or improving answer quality without manual tuning—practical for production search, RAG, and assistant systems.
visual_elements: Flowchart: Query + target (accuracy/budget) → selector → pipeline config → retrieval + synthesis → answer
Pareto plot: cost vs accuracy with highlighted chosen config per query showing movement along the frontier
Catalog matrix: icons/tiles showing configuration dimensions (LLM size, retriever, #docs, #hops, synthesis) and sampled options
Before/After example: concrete query with static vs selected config, showing cost saved and accuracy retained/improved
paper_title: Natural Language Query to Configuration for Retrieval Agents
paper_authors: Melissa Z. Pan, Negar Arabzadeh, Mathew Jacob, Fiodar Kazhamiaka, Esha Choukse
